part_title: Network ACLs, Flow Logs, VPC Peering and Private Connectivity

scenes.title: Network ACLs versus Security Groups
scenes.narration: This diagram places Network ACLs at the subnet boundary and security groups around the individual elastic network interfaces. Read the comparison table. An ACL is stateless, so ingress and egress rules must each allow the required traffic, including return packets. ACL rules are numbered, evaluated in order, and can allow or deny. A security group is stateful: return traffic from an established allowed connection is automatically permitted, and security group rules normally specify allows rather than explicit denies. When debugging a database timeout, examine source and destination security groups along with the subnet ACLs; an ACL can block an ephemeral return port even if port 443 is allowed in one direction. The controls complement each other rather than replacing one another. In an AI architecture, use security groups for narrowly scoped application-to-database communication and ACLs where subnet-level restrictions add value. Avoid indiscriminately opening all ports simply to make an error disappear.

scenes.title: VPC Flow Logs
scenes.narration: The example follows network traffic through an EC2 instance's elastic network interface. VPC Flow Logs captures connection metadata, which can be delivered to CloudWatch Logs or S3 for analysis. Compare the sample ACCEPT record for an HTTPS flow with the REJECT record for an incoming SSH attempt. Fields identify source and destination IPs, ports, timestamps, action and status; they do not contain the full packet payload or a user's model prompt. An ACCEPT record does not prove the application successfully processed a request, and a REJECT record doesn't necessarily explain which individual rule caused the block. The slide's right-hand workflow suggests using Logs Insights or Athena for queries and metric filters for suspicious patterns. For a GenAI API, flow logs help distinguish blocked network traffic from a successful TCP connection followed by an IAM AccessDenied or Bedrock throttling response. Combine network evidence with application logs and tracing to find the actual failure.

scenes.title: VPC peering
scenes.narration: This slide shows three VPC address ranges and a peering connection between VPC A and VPC B. Follow the paired route tables: A needs a route toward B's CIDR through the peering connection, and B needs a return route toward A. Security controls still decide which workloads can communicate. VPC C is included to demonstrate the important limitation. Even if B has another peering connection to C, A cannot use B as a transit router to reach C. VPC peering is non-transitive. Address ranges also cannot overlap for ordinary peering. For a handful of VPCs requiring direct private routes, peering is manageable. For complex many-to-many topologies, consider Transit Gateway. If the business requirement is simply to reach one shared AI service, PrivateLink may offer more targeted service-level access than routing entire networks together. The key is choosing connectivity to match the actual trust boundary.

scenes.title: VPC endpoints
scenes.narration: The diagram contrasts a gateway endpoint with an interface endpoint. Gateway endpoints support S3 and DynamoDB through entries in the subnet route tables, so private workloads can reach those services without a NAT internet path. Interface endpoints instead create private network interfaces in selected subnets and provide PrivateLink connectivity to supported AWS APIs, including appropriate Bedrock endpoints. The cost panels help with design decisions: gateway endpoints generally have no separate hourly endpoint charge, while interface endpoints commonly incur hourly and data-processing fees. The endpoint's existence alone does not guarantee a successful request. The workload still needs IAM permissions, the correct service and Region, appropriate endpoint policy where supported, security group rules for interface endpoints and working private DNS or explicit endpoint configuration. When troubleshooting a model call, test name resolution, network reachability and authorisation separately. This slide teaches private access to specific managed services, not a blanket permission to reach everything inside AWS.

scenes.title: Site-to-Site VPN and Direct Connect
scenes.narration: The left path creates an IPsec Site-to-Site VPN between on-premises customer networking equipment and an AWS gateway, using internet-based connectivity with encrypted tunnels. The right path uses AWS Direct Connect to provide a dedicated connection through a Direct Connect location. Compare the rows below. VPN can often be deployed faster, while Direct Connect can provide more predictable bandwidth for sustained enterprise traffic and typically needs more provisioning work. A crucial distinction is that Direct Connect is private connectivity, not automatically end-to-end encryption. If encryption is required, plan the appropriate overlay or tunnel. Both approaches need routing, firewall policy, authentication and redundant connections for high availability. For hybrid AI, the network may carry private source documents, API requests or data feeds, so performance, data residency, cost and encryption requirements matter. Choose based on measured workload characteristics rather than treating either option as universally superior.
